thread:
Sam Ramos: Quick sync — ran into a blindspot in observability for streaming aborts. When a client aborts during a mid-request handoff we only see a generic CLOSE from the proxy, no origin of the abort (client vs upstream vs healthcheck).
Jia Chen: Yeah we've seen that in a couple incidents. Hard to tell if it's network flake, user cancel, or our preemption.
Leo Patel: Do you have an example trace/log snippet?
Sam Ramos: Pasting a sanitized log fragment — the trace id is there but abort cause is missing, and trailers are absent:
```
2024-09-01T16:21:03.123Z edge-proxy[req=abc123] INFO "stream closed" latency=1204ms trace=tr-9c7f
2024-09-01T16:21:03.124Z upstream[req=abc123] INFO "upstream connection reset by peer" code=ECONNRESET
2024-09-01T16:21:03.124Z edge-proxy[req=abc123] INFO "request terminated" status=499
```
Sam Ramos: Notice we have status 499 but nothing that maps 499->client-cancel vs our preempt.
Maya Ortiz: 499 is noisy because different layers set it. We need a structured abort_reason in logs/traces.
Jia Chen: Agreed. Two approaches: 1) enrich headers/trailers with abort-cause ("x-rw-abort: client-cancel") or 2) emit a side-channel telemetry event before teardown with fields {req, trace, abort_reason}.
Leo Patel: Trailers are attractive but not always available (HTTP/1 clients, some proxies strip). Also, if stream already closed we can't send it. Side-channel event seems more reliable.
Jia Chen: Side-channel means one more RPC to observability — cost + potential racing (if process crashes before event). But it's durable if we buffer to local spool.
Sam Ramos: What about adding an abort span to tracing (so it shows up in traces and can be correlated)? That way Jaeger/OTLP will contain the cause.
Leo Patel: That maps well. We can annotate the span with span.set_attribute("rw.abort_reason", "client_cancel") and emit a short log line. If span exporter drops, at least local logs have structured fields.
Maya Ortiz: We should standardize abort_reason enum: client_cancel, upstream_reset, healthcheck_kill, preemptive_evict, internal_error. Keep small.
Jia Chen: Implementation plan: short-term patch — add structured log field abort_reason when known, and emit a tracing span tag. Medium-term RFC -> side-channel event for cases where abort reason is inferred post-facto.
Sam Ramos: Also need to decide where inference lives. Edge should supply best-effort: look at error codes, socket events, and internal state machine. Avoid leaking user PII in reasons.
Leo Patel: Security note: don't include full headers or user tokens. Only opaque request id and reason enum. We'll gate verbose debug behind a feature flag (edge.telemetry.abort_debug=true).
Jia Chen: Sketch of change to edge handler (pseudocode):
```
// on terminal event
reason = infer_abort_reason(conn_event, upstream_event, signal)
logger.info("request.term", {req_id, trace, status, abort_reason: reason})
tracer.active_span().set_attribute("rw.abort_reason", reason)
```
Maya Ortiz: For streaming specifically, we should capture last-sent-offset and whether we flushed trailers. That helps debugging partial-deliveries. Add fields: last_offset, trailers_sent:true/false.
Sam Ramos: Good call. How about sampling? We can't flood traces for every 499. Propose: sample 1% by default and 100% when status >=500 or when the request is from customer with dedicated plan (configurable).
Jia Chen: Also add an ops endpoint to replay the inferred abort reasoning for a given req_id (read-only) so SREs can fetch the debug trail if sampling missed.
Leo Patel: Action items:
- Open short RFC for structured abort_reason + tracing attribute (owner: Leo)
- Jia to implement the quick log + span tag patch behind feature flag (branch then canary)
- Sam to add unit/integration tests for infer_abort_reason heuristics
- Maya to define enum & observability schema and update dashboards/alerts
- ops-bot link: deploy-preview will run on canary cluster -> @ops-bot please schedule canary after merge
Maya Ortiz: I'll draft the enum doc now and put it in the observability repo.
Jia Chen: One more thought — for clients that support trailers, we could include a short trailer `rw-abort: <enum>` to preserve provenance end-to-end when possible. No sensitive info, just the enum.
Sam Ramos: That gives users more visibility too. Ok let's not block on trailers for MVP. Follow-ups tracked in the RFC.
Leo Patel: I'll file the RFC with a design section and backward-compat notes. Target: decide within 2 weeks.
Sam Ramos: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll create the JIRA tasks and assign them. :thumbsup:
